projectSummary: This is a direct contradiction of the later dumbbell-fly comparison: where one study found higher pectoralis activation in the press, this one found no significant difference in activation level and a difference only in the time the muscle was active. Both are carried, and neither is preferred.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: Abstract-only; twelve mixed-sex participants of varied experience.
Non-significance in a sample of twelve cannot distinguish no difference from not enough information (rule H2).

study.intervention: barbell bench press; dumbbell bench press; dumbbell fly
study.population: Twelve college-age men and women with various degrees of lifting experience performed three repetitions at their six-repetition maximum in the barbell bench press, dumbbell bench press and dumbbell fly, while EMG of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid was recorded during the concentric phase.

title: Electromyographic activity of the pectoralis major and anterior deltoid muscles during three upper-body lifts.
